public_rationale: The records support the narrower observation that OpenAI and Anthropic were unprofitable in 2024. They do not settle whether falling inference costs helped their finances. A company can benefit from lower costs and still lose money. Calling the whole statement supported would therefore treat an unproved financial-effect claim as established.
limitations: The company scope and reporting period require interpretation.
Anthropic's filing uses GAAP figures, while the post relies on press estimates.
Later financial improvements cannot establish what was happening during 2024.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: None of these generative AI companies are profitable, and despite repeated claims that the cost of inference is coming down, that doesn't appear to be helping them.

statement.excerpt: None of these companies are profitable, and despite repeated claims that "the cost of inference is coming down" (the thing that happens when you prompt the model to do something) it doesn't appear to be helping them.

from_speaker: None of these companies are profitable
the cost of inference is coming down
it doesn't appear to be helping them
our_interpretation: These companies refers to OpenAI and Anthropic, the immediate subjects of the passage, rather than every company selling generative AI.
I use calendar 2024, the latest completed annual period available for reporting before the post and the period discussed immediately beforehand.
Profitable means positive company-wide net income, not revenue growth or a positive product margin.
The second clause concerns an observable financial benefit from lower inference costs. Remaining unprofitable does not by itself establish that no benefit occurred.
The hedge is not a conditional forecast and supplies no future deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Both companies had nonpositive 2024 net income, and comparable evidence shows that lower inference costs had not materially improved their financial performance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Either company had positive comparable net income, or reliable period-specific evidence establishes a material financial improvement attributable to lower inference costs.
